messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: P1 high tail latency on inference cluster (region-us-west). Alerts fired: latency_p99_inference > 5s, error_rate spike. Started 2026-03-17T10:12:09Z

elaine: I’m on it. joining

samir: seeing large queue depth on gpu-pool-3, workers stuck with long KV cache loads. starting scale-up and checking recent deploys

ben: scaled gpu-pool-3 +2 nodes (now 12). applied emergency route to fallback-model-v1 for non-critical routes: `/api/generate/low-priority`

elaine: thanks. rolling a partial traffic shift for webhooks to fallback, will monitor error budget. @ops-bot can you verify autoscaler logs?

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaleUp event -> group gpu-pool-3 increased from 10 -> 12 at 2026-03-17T10:15:03Z; reason: sustained queue depth > 200 for 2m

samir: after scale-up p99 dropped from ~7.8s -> ~3.2s for most routes, but a handful of long traces remain (model kv-cache miss storms).

elaine: mitigation checklist: 1) keep scaled nodes for +30m, 2) keep fallback routing for low-priority traffic, 3) collect traces for stubborn requests, 4) post-incident dashboard and alert tuning.

ben: capturing k8s pod logs to s3: `infra/tools/logdump --since 2026-03-17T10:10 --label gpu-pool=gpu-pool-3 --out s3://redwood-debug/paging-3123456789/`

samir: creating a short trace set in jaeger for the firehose requests, grabbing sample ids and attaching to the incident ticket.

elaine: handoff in 10m to @marco (next oncall). leaving a summary in the incident ticket. current customer impact: small percentage of requests to some routes had >4s latency for ~18m window, no systemic error-rate increase beyond transient 2-3x for 2m. prioritizing latency/experience over 100% availability.

marco: thanks — I’ll own the postmortem and dashboard follow-up. can we keep a list of noisy alerts that should be tuned?

elaine: list so far: `latency_p99_inference` (alerting per-host), `queue_depth_high` (firing on low-count spikes), `kv_cache_miss_rate` (noises when model warmups occur). also `model_fallback_count` alerts are noisy when we intentionally route.

marco: noted. for the retrospective dashboard I want the following panels: 1) Golden signals overview (p50/p90/p99 latency, error rate, throughput) 2) Alert timeline (alerts firing vs acknowledgement) 3) Autoscaler events and pool size over time 4) Per-route fallback counts and traffic shifts 5) KV cache hitrate and evictions 6) Top slow traces + link to jaeger 7) Cost/slot utilization during incident

samir: +1. propose drilldowns: clicking a panel opens filtered dashboard for that route / node, and a quick filter for timeframe (incident window).

ben: sample promql for p99 panel: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))` — need to group by model variant and route.

marco: awesome. I’ll open a PR in infra/grafana/dashboards: `retrospective/paging_incident_3123456789.json` and assign to @elaine for review. target: PR by EOD, merge next day.

elaine: will add a short alert tuning proposal in the PR: 1) change `latency_p99_inference` to use cluster-aggregate with a secondary per-route warning (reduce noisy per-host alerts), 2) convert `queue_depth_high` to a rate-based alert (sustained increase for 5m), 3) add suppression when `fallback_routing_active == true` to avoid intentional routing noise.

ops-bot: NOTE: there is an existing alert runbook link for `latency_p99_inference` -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-p99

samir: for the Grafana panels I’ll add queries and example drilldown links. suggested panel titles and queries attached in the PR description. small example: drilldown url `https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/retrospective/paging?var-route=$route&from=$__from&to=$__to`

marco: assigning tasks: ben (logs + sample export), samir (queries + panels), elaine (alert tuning writeup + review), me (PR author + postmortem). ETA: postmortem draft in 48h, dashboard PR in 24h.

elaine: thank you team. I’ll keep the incident ticket updated with final customer impact numbers and timeline. closing oncall thread. :white_check_mark:
